title: The Worst Journey in the World
subtitle: We hope someone found joy in the ride, even if just for a moment.

items.text: The Worst Journey in the World
They trudge upward through the deep snow.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Great Mother Spirit ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'm almost there. Just-Just a little farther.
Unsteady and fresh snowpack makes it nearly impossible to keep a steady footing.
Each step comes with a wobble as she rebalances herself.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Traveling on foot was never a good choice for an expedition. Evil Snow Monsters!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: First sled dogs, then mad critters. *grunt*
Her ice ax slams deep into the packed snow.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And now endless daylight. Endless glaring sun.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Is all this because of that ritual? What the heck are those Snow Monsters trying to do?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen, how long until we reach the ruins?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I don't know. I-I don't know.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Careful. Something's coming.
A low, thunderous rumble vibrates the ground beneath their boots.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: An earthquake?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No, no, no, no, no, not an earthquake. Lower your body. Whatever you do, don't lose your footing.
The black substance surging beneath the ice shatters the frozen layers, erupting out over a distant ridge.
The creeping darkness spreads downhill, fracturing the earth as it advances toward the cluster of research stations.

items.speaker: Sled Dog
items.text: Woof ...
The polar wind carries faint, helpless howls from the same sled dogs that had chased them yesterday.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The sled dogs, they're smart. They avoided the cracks very intelligently.
Nautika murmurs under her breath, unable to hide her concern.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nautika, you're a capable reindeer-and-dog trainer, right?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Oh, no-no. I-I really don't think that's a good idea. They tried to kill us yesterday.
Her protests die on her lips until, finally, she swallows up her remaining objections.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: W-Well, maybe I can give it a try. They might still have some sense.
On hands and knees, she scrambles up the slope.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But it's been a while since I last gave any orders. W-What if they don't listen to me?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Come on, Nautika. Time to "hit the drum."
Her eyes widen, then she nods.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: *gulp* You're right.
A long, clear whistle pierces the air from Nautika's chapped and cold lips as she waves her arms wildly.
In the distance, the frenzied sled dogs take notice and gradually quiet.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Hike!
She sweeps her arm backward in a grand gesture.
Chaotic snow-scrabbling sounds carry from afar, the long-unruly dog team now stirring to command.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You can do this, Nautika. Try again.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Hike!
A pause hangs thick in the air.
The sound of barking dogs gets nearer as approaching paws churn the snow into a rushing tide of powder.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Haw! Easy!
Nautika presses her palms downward.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Get ready, everyone!
Her legs are shaking, but her eyes glitter with exhilaration.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, are we really going to do this?
The dog team is nearly upon them, still half-wild as they speed forward. Yet in a single swinging motion, Nautika pulls herself up and over the top of the lead sled dog.
Ms. Radio rustles, nearly tumbling from her perch.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Oh, holy mother of—What are we doing?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I-I have no idea.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Straight ahead. Straight ahead! Hahaha!
The dogs charge downslope without hesitation, ignoring any potential pitfalls that may be hidden in the mist.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Oh—Oh, right.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Pet them around the head and neck. That will help you bond with them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I suppose that makes sense.
Fingers brush over a sled dog's head, coarse yet soft fur slipping between them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I hope Ulrich has come across friends as reliable as these.
Nautika presses low, burying her face in the soft fur behind the dog's neck.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I did it. I did it.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: These are the biggest sled dogs I've ever seen.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Lieutenant, we have spotted a suspicious unit.
Moldir grabs the intercom and pulls it close, listening for messages cutting through the whiteout.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: A schooner has come ashore due east. It appears to be alone.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Team One and Two, come with me. Team Three, stay and keep watch.
Former Zeno Sentinel Unit Station
With mutual trust, the disciplined soldiers move in perfect and silent synchronization, slipping behind a natural barrier near the ice shelf.
With an anchor's splash, the schooner drifts up against the icy shore.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Target presents as unarmed, but we can't rule anything out yet.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Team One, follow me.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Team Two, stand by at Bunker A2. Keep your eyes on the coast. We don't want to be caught unaware if they send reinforcements.
Her hand held over her firearm, Moldir leads the infantry squad forward in measured strides.
Blinded by the whiteout, the schooner's passengers march themselves obliviously into the waiting ambush.
Sea sickness, whiteout, and judging by the trembling compass pointer, something's messing with the magnetic field here.
Boss, you're probably the least suitable person in the world to be doing this mission.
Shoot. I can already hear my silicon dioxide crackling.
Find a windproof bunker. I need to reapply the hydrophobic and cold-resistant coatings.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Now!
Muzzles snap up in unison, all aimed at the Awakened and his guard.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Sergeant Frekhtman, take two soldiers with you and search the schooner for any other threats.
At her signal, three armed soldiers advance through the swirling snow.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: You are under arrest.
An ID badge hangs conspicuously on the chest of the figure before them.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Laplace researcher.
The ferrofluid inside his head morphs through multiple shapes at blinding speed.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: That uniform ... Are you from Zeno? There must have been a mix-up. We have the official approval of the St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: After a prolonged silence, the guard interrupts his testimony.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Boss, I've seen their faces hanging in the Hall of Merit. So, unless they're ghosts ...

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: We've just stumbled upon the rebels.
Moldir closes her eyes briefly, as if avoiding a particular word.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: What is your purpose here?
Ulrich raises his right hand to the white mist, his left remaining in his pocket.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: It's none of your business. All you need to know is that we're not a threat to you.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: We came here alone, no backup.
A voice comes over the intercom.

items.speaker: Intercom
items.text: Lieutenant, the schooner is cleared. Only an unarmed sailor on board. The outpost confirmed that they haven't spotted any other ship.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Lower your gun, Lieutenant. We're not a threat.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We're just here to play a tune.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: A poor excuse, researcher.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Please head back to where you came from. Now is not the best time to play sing-song in Antarctica.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I'm not leaving.
The Awakened raises his left hand, a grenade gripped within it—the pin already loose—the pressure of his fingers on the lever all that stands between the striker and the fuse.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Fall back!
Moldir barks her squad back and advances alone, her firearm held high and steady.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Calm down, sir. You're a researcher. Perhaps you should stick to the pursuit of knowledge and leave the explosives handling to me.
She locks onto the tiny silver lettering stamped on the grenade.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I know the owner of this grenade.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: After the first "Storm," all Zeno equipment was codified under a particular numbering system and distributed among the platoons.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: But the number on this grenade belongs to someone special. Someone in an independent team.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Someone who has a unique code on all her equipment, including her famous Su-01ве flying device.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: A Slav.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: So, you've been in contact with Team Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: And what if I have?
From the swirling pace of his ferrofluid, it's clear he's taken the question badly.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: So the weapon that was supposed to protect me is the very thing that gave me away. How ironic!
With a wave, Moldir signals her squad to hold position while she holsters her gun, then grasps the grenade with one hand.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Are you out of your minds? This is a real grenade, you know. Powerful as 200 grams of TNT.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Что было, то и будет.
The pin whips back into place. The spring retracts. Everything resets to its factory-new state.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Your arcane skill?
She offers no explanation as she wrenches the now-harmless grenade from Ulrich's grip.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: For the last time, what is your purpose here?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Is it about the Timekeeper, about Vertin?
